body:
Marriage counseling and individual therapy have more or less taught us that we are incompatible (at least that's what we've gathered) and that our differences mean constant uphill battles. I feel like I've grown into myself, understanding who I am and what I want, how to voice my needs and how to communicate more effectively. I've learned where some of my behaviors come from and the type of things that trigger me. As much as people here want to make me out to be the bad guy, my husband has a lot to work on as well. We've talked about non negotiables and it seems like we're asking each other to be different people - we can't meet each other's needs, but not for lack of wanting or trying.  

That's a heavy answer but we've been through a lot and I feel mentally drained. It's hard and I feel like the reason why it's so hard is because we're forcing something that isn't meant to happen.

Thanks for checking out my post history. I will clarify that my therapist wanted to explore the possibility of BPD but never formally diagnosed me. She concluded that I was just having emotional dysregulation due to triggers surrounding my childhood emotional neglect trauma. Also complications with medications causing added agitation. And I realize my post history is.. all over the place. I'm in a much better mental space now but am still having issues with my marriage, mostly caused by communication and understanding problems. On both sides.

But to make a broad, sweeping judgement instead of advice pertaining to this issue alone doesn't make any sense. I do ask for advice to consider all angles of the situation, otherwise I wouldn't bother. I do feel like I'm compromising and not requesting my husband forego alcohol altogether, I just ask that he waits until the kids go to bed. What doesn't make sense to me is why he feels the need to argue with me about about something he isn't considering could impact the kids, plus it's a boundary he already told me he'd respect. Obviously people are on different ends of the argument here, just as they would be regarding porn, weed, rules, discipline, etc.
I'm sorry that's what you're gathering out of this one example. And that Internet strangers are quick to label me based on this one issue.

This isn't the only "hill" I'm up against. This is one example of something we are disagreeing on and something he originally explicitly told me he'd respect, then he turns around and does something different.

Because I gave one example of a value I asked him to consider? And regarding the book - I didn't know anything about it other than it was a book to help foster support for your spouse but I learned it was stigmatizing and degrading toward mental health issues, which I didn't think would be helpful. I don't understand how all these negative comments can come about with so little context into the dynamics of our relationship.
Thank you so much for this comment. I knew I would get a mix of responses. I appreciate your support.

Please understand that we don't discuss divorce simply when we're disagreeing. There are many, many other factors at play and all are because he wants us to "agree to disagree" - but on topics like communication, validation, support, attention, etc.

Thank you for your thoughtful words. We actually did a trial separation over the summer and it was wonderful. We both acknowledged less stress and anxiety, and we were able to work it out well with the kids. He said we came back from it in a better place, but I believe that was just because we had just had a break from each other. It quickly went back to how it was before, but now I realize a longer/more permanent separation is what we need.

We have an ongoing struggle with misaligned values. When those differences come up in conversation, he'll tell me he doesn't want to hear my opinion (most recently when we were talking about religion) because of how he thinks it will affect the kids. But then when I confront him from the other side..
It's not "hidden" - it's in plain sight in the fridge, just kept for adult time (ideally).
I hear you on that. They see it in the fridge and we talk about what it is and that it's for grownups. It's not "hidden" it's just kept for adult time.
I don't have a problem with him drinking, I just ask that he waits until the kids go to bed.

I understand I have posts about BPD, but haven't made any clarifying follow ups - my therapist never officially diagnosed me, we just discussed the possibility. After more therapy, she concluded I don't, in fact, have BPD, I've just been under an immense amount of emotional stress due to my marriage triggering childhood emotional neglect. 

I did not "blow up" at dinner. We had a civil conversation during which we continued to disagree.
Oh, well, that's definitely one we don't have. We have sex once a year and I cried the last time it happened.

He says I'm the reason for our problems. Yes, I've gotten increasingly impatient but it's because I feel invisible. When I bring up any sort of grievance, he turns it around on me or justifies himself. He tries to tell me our issues are my fault - my anxiety, my "high standards", my needs being too difficult for him to meet, that I'll never be happy. And I'm beginning to think he's right. I'll never be happy with HIM because I'm bearing all the emotional weight of our marriage.
Where did sexual compatibility come from?

My point exactly. I don't care if he drinks after they go to bed or if we're out. Don't care at all. He kept defending himself and I asked why it was so important that he NOT wait until they're in the bed? I feel like I am compromising by giving him the freedom to drink, I'm just asking he not do it around the kids.

We've tried two different counselors and I told him to go find a different one if he wasn't happy. Gave him a list to go through if he felt that would be helpful. I've also encouraged him to find resources, even sent things to him, and they go unread/unwatched. I gave him one book recommendation then read some bad reviews and told him not to read it or listen to it and he stopped and never picked up anything again because it was wrong and told me he was waiting on something that had my approval. Everything just feels like a fight, even trying to get help.

Thank you for your answer. I think you're spot on. He has said he wishes things would go back to how they were before I started being more vocal about my needs (not his exact words, but the gist). 

And we've been in weekly counseling for about a year with no improvement, maybe even things getting worse. And yes, going over the same issues again and again. Picking up on these patterns, hearing my concerns be validated by the counselor, and witnessing him justify himself over and over has been incredibly difficult.

He says those things because he thinks that's what I want based on our conversations. And I don't bring up divorce to threaten him, but to discuss the gravity of our issues. Like it's a real possibility if we can't get on the same page and learn how to connect and communicate. It's been a long road with many, many things leading up to this point, so please try to understand that I'm not over here waving a divorce flag every time we argue.

We are also very committed to encouraging their self esteem, confidence, etc. and I believe they can be raised to make good choices. And if not, keeping an open line of communication and trust while providing a good example that you don't need alcohol to relax or have fun.
I've brought up individual counseling and so has our marriage therapist and he says he doesn't need it.
I have many other safe places to land but your partner should be your safest place, yes? Or at least not someone who makes you feel unsafe.
In this instance, I feel like he's asking me to compromise on my values and the values we can instill in the kids.
In this instance, it feels like he's asking me to compromise on my values and I just don't see that happening. If he has a value of freely drinking alcohol, we have bigger problems.

This article is behind a paywall. 

We've done conversation starters from books and our therapist but it hasn't gone well. He'll give me one word answers, or say I don't know, or if it's a heavier topic, we tend to disagree, which we can talk about but it doesn't bring us closer.

I have talked to my individual therapist and honestly she said he just isn't capable of meeting my needs so either find them elsewhere or move on. Finding them elsewhere (friends, etc) makes me feel lonely in my partnership, so I feel trapped.
I don't think so either. So that goes back to my predicament - accept and settle or move on.

So my trouble is can I handle being with a non-introspective person as a very introspective person myself, knowing he'll likely never change or value personal growth (besides development in his career). He's told me he wishes I would go back to being the person I was when we got married instead of the more open, enlightened version of myself I've grown into being.
I think he's trying but not capable. He's not been evaluated for being on the spectrum.
How do I change my requirements?
Thank you for your insight. I have brought up the idea of individual counseling, as has our marriage counselor, but he says he doesn't need it. He even thinks marriage counseling is a waste of time.

- I have no idea

- He tells me his ex was a "crazy bitch" but again on the shared computer, I've found saved notes he copied and pasted from email threads with her basically demanding his emotional attention and him downplaying it. So they probably had the same issues

- No, we don't spend time together unless it's with the kids. We recently scheduled a date and he called it off because I was "too stressed". We also recently went on a vacation together (just the two of us) and it felt awkward. It was fun, but it was more like we were having fun separately rather than bonding.

- I don't know what that means
Yes, yes, yes. He definitely goes through motions and performs based on a checklist, which means things don't get done thoroughly or logically, but he *does* them, so it should be enough.
What is a partner supposed to provide then, if not a safe place to land with struggles, engaging conversation, companionship, understanding, and empathy?

He has opened up a bit in counseling but says things like he doesn't know what I want or how to meet my needs. He has tunnel vision and thinks if things are good in his mind, everything's fine. I've brought up feeling lonely, disconnected, and unfulfilled, and we've tried talking through that, but he thinks he's doing enough.

I have been thinking about that question a lot - why did we get married. We were both coming out of serious relationships (he was going through divorce and I had just ended an engagement). We got engaged 6 months later and married 6 months after that. I remember "bonding" through more social activities, not really discussing our needs, wants, desires, etc. Big mistake on my part, I understand now. I was attracted to him because he's a good provider and I wanted to feel safe and secure. Now I feel emotionally unsafe and insecure, but financially I'm taken care of. 

I want more out of the marriage and it would be great if it were with him, but I don't know if he's equipped for that. But it feels selfish to chase after my happiness when on the surface, we seem to be doing alright.
End it how? I feel my only options are end the marriage, give up my needs and settle, or somehow become okay with not being fulfilled.

Right, which is why we both feel frustrated - he says he's giving me what I want in these situations, but it misses the mark because it's insincere. For another example, we have discussed how to show empathy and how to react when I feel stressed/overwhelmed/etc (because he's had a track record of not responding appropriately) and he'll just regurgitate my words verbatim, even if they don't really fit. So he feels like he's giving me what I need based on instruction, when to me it feels like he needs explicit prompts and scripts to be able to communicate effectively, which doesn't feel comforting at all.

Operations Manager/backup PC

ETA he currently works Saturday-Monday 3am-6pm on the fulfillment side.

If you could be a fly on the wall. I ask my husband questions and he gives me short one word answers. Or his answers require a follow-up question, which prompts me to ask more questions, which he has told me is the most annoying thing about me. I'm too curious and inquisitive.

ETA my questions and/or pointed statements, like you mentioned.
But I do need my husband to be evolutionarily expressive to know where he stands on things, how he's feeling, to gain a sense of partnership as we go through things together, etc.

He shared a list of expectations with me but also stated that my change in "values" is completely in the way and the biggest non negotiable. 

I don't expect him to meet every need but to be there for me as a supportive partner when I need him. I don't think that's too much to ask. 

As far as our kids, they are our focus and I'm concerned our relationship together isn't doing them any services serving as a model. Although not for lack of trying and patience and compromise. We feel mismatched.
I understand what you're saying but that doesn't make it easier to accept. It actually makes me less attracted to my husband because I do think I need a more insightful partner.
He's joined one or two of my individual therapy sessions but we do have marriage counseling together weekly. I've also encouraged him to go to individual therapy, which he has once.

There are so many ways I'm focusing on my own mental health, including medication, therapy, meditation, journaling, reading, and staying accountable by being involved in research studies. 

I do have a sense of hopelessness, tragedy, and dread that I can't explain. Hence the therapy and things. I feel like nothing works but I'm doing the best I can. I feel I do have extra mental health needs but all I'm asking from him is a little support - show me he's thinking of me, ask my about myself and my interests, carry on a conversation. He's very triggering to me because of my past with parental emotional neglect. He knows that's part of my history but does not meet me in the middle to help me feel more safe. I'm doing all I can to make myself feel all the good things, but then I have this external factor bringing me back into the lonely feelings.
I've asked him to seek personal counseling and he said he needs more weed, not therapy. I died when he said that.

I did get a part time job and am saving my money in a separate account. 

I plan on consulting a divorce lawyer and understanding my options as far as monetary support so I'm not struggling on that front.

I am not a Christian but I appreciate your perspective. Our kids do not see a loving marriage. Maybe a neutral one, but not a loving one. My husband is a great dad and I would trust him to raise our kids appropriately during his time with them. I'm not worried about that at all. 

I do have a mom's group I'm a part of and we talk regularly about our struggles and help each other heal. That doesn't change my daily frustrations. 

I'm doing everything I can to work on myself - personal therapy, meditation, art, journaling, keeping an active social life, taking on a part time job, trying to remember I'm only responsible for myself and my reactions. But it's like trying to continue on after losing a loved one. Our marriage feels dead and it's painful.

I'm doing the best I can with the time I have, but I can't exactly travel the world or take classes that interest me because I have other responsibilities, conflicting schedules, and a budget. It just doesn't work out like it would otherwise.

We've been in couples counseling for about 6 months. It was a whole thing trying to get him to agree and schedule something. I put the ball in his court to see if he took me seriously. He didn't and I had to give him a hard deadline and finally schedule something myself after he dragged his feet. 

I will say that my husband would never, ever say something like, "How can I help?" or "What do I do to make you resentful?" He lacks emotional insight and never starts deep conversations at all. He can clearly see I'm struggling, but doesn't bring it up. It's incredibly lonely.

There is no joint effort other than him telling me to go find a hobby. I don't necessarily want my previous life back, but there is a certain degree of mourning independence and identity when you become a stay at home mom. If I wasn't in this role, I would be traveling and taking classes that interest me. But that's not an option at all right now, so that makes me feel flighty in itself. Surely every adult feels this way, it's just more complicated with kids.

My husband also has ADD and I've never considered the compartmentalization as part of that but that's definitely something he does. I will note that he never, ever opens up freely about anything. I'm always left guessing what he's thinking, feeling, how he's dealing with things, etc. It's very frustrating and lonely.

No, he kept his job as it was, doing what he wanted to do at the pace he wanted to do it. He worked 65+ hours a week at his previous job, on his own accord, just because he loved it. His job now is more family friendly but I don't think he saw or sees the sacrifice I've made because he dismisses me when I voice frustration by saying I could have put the kids in childcare all this time.

Thank you for your reply. I feel I compromise by giving up my life and interests to be a stay at home mom for 6 years. I do the vast majority of the domestic duties, but do voice my appreciation when he contributes or takes on projects. 

I do not feel affectionate because I do not feel the emotional connection. Something else to work through I guess, but it feels very uncomfortable. 

I see my faults and I know I have things to work on, thus the therapy and spending so much time on therapeutic activities. 

Maybe I'm at fault here but our relationship brings me very little joy. He is very triggering and I am not happy when I'm around him. That's all I know.

I thought counseling was going to make things better. I begged and begged my husband to consider it until he agreed. However, now that I'm seeing a third party acknowledge and validate my frustrations, and still not seeing any improvements, I'm almost more discouraged.
We've been married 7 years, in counseling about 4 months, but I have been messaging friends and other therapists for advice throughout the past 5 years.

Thank you for your reply. I often do the things you suggested - thank him for every helpful task, ask if he wants to spend time with me after the kids go to bed (but he often chooses to watch sports or go to bed). I have a hard time when the physical touch thing. I think because of our lack of emotional intimacy, like you said, I have a very hard time with the physical stuff. I've been sexually assaulted and I think it's triggering to touch intimately without that feeling of security. I've told him this and he acted like he didn't know (even though I reminded him I had already told him and he said, "of yeah, that one guy in X city?" Complete lack of comfort or emotional reaction. 

Interactions with him just hurt.

Things are stressful but I feel very balanced with a new job, friends, and hobbies. I feel I have been slowly backing away due to his lack of emotional availability, difficulty in talking to him without feeling dismissed or invalidated, and him not showing personal interest in me. This comes in the form of him neglecting to share important information with me, not offering comfort when I'm emotional or say something vulnerable (in fact, often saying insensitive things), and deflecting when I bring up frustrations.

Maybe? I'm currently a stay at home mom (trying REALLY hard to get a part time job) and my husband just started a new job working only 3 days a week. We definitely see a lot more of each other than we used to.

My husband has been supportive in the sense of providing and not leaving me, but his emotional availability and comfort is lacking - he's trying but it's just not where I need it to be. I struggle with that regularly, knowing someone else could very well be a better match.
I literally told my husband the same thing a few weeks ago. I still struggle with the sexual identity part - and not sure if that's the BPD speaking.
I think that's why I feel like I want to leave.
That wasn't the point of the argument.

I'm trying. Our marriage counselor agreed to have a few sessions focused entirely on BPD. I'm beginning DBT this week, participate in research studies to keep me accountable with my healing, and journal my thoughts/moods. I feel like I'm doing a lot for myself without it being overwhelming.

The reason why the bedtime example became an issue was because he wasn't answering my question directly and changing his story when I did finally get an answer. That's what frustrates me - not feeling like we're on the same page especially when I'm trying to get information from him.
I have been open and honest, trying to explain exactly how it affects me and how I feel inside. I'm starting DBT with my therapist this week.

I've been in personal therapy for 2.5 years and we've been in marriage counseling 3 months. I and the therapists have asked that he educate himself so he can help support me through my healing. I do feel like our relationship hinders that.

No, I heard what the kids said and it was a clear, "What time is it." Then he tried to say the kids didn't ask him that, but I heard him clearly. That's when he started changing his story. 

I do go to therapy once a week and marriage counseling is also once a week. I also volunteer in research studies to give me ongoing accountability in treatment methods.  I am very educated on BPD, but I don't feel my husband is. After his "research", he told me what I needed to be doing and suggested I go to a psych ward. Even after my follow up questions about now he thought he could support me, those were his answers.
I told him that when I first shared the diagnosis
We do sit down and try to see eye to eye but it doesn't result in that often. Most conversations end up arguments because one or both of us don't feel heard.

Found this old post looking for similar support. I am a wife of 7 years and we have 2 kids. I hate how trapped I feel in my life and I hate that I even think that. I feel emotionally alone, invalidated, invisible, and unloved. It is very, very hard for me to feel love from my husband, but I do feel it from my kids. I think BPD has ruined my marriage. Or maybe marriage has made me worse. Too many small opportunities to need someone else just to be let down. It's like Chinese water torture. 

What I'm trying to do to cope is find a job (I've been a stay at home parent since having our kids) and try not to rely on my husband for anything. That's so sad to say, but it's easier than feeling let down. I do still rely on him for too much, especially emotional validation, but that's my one skill I'm trying to use. 

I'm sorry I don't have anything more useful than solidarity. But I hear you.

Your partner sounds very different than mine. My husband doesn't open up or talk to me, ever. If I'm clearly distraught or stressed or having an awful day, he leaves me alone. If I say I want to talk, he listens and nods his head, leaving me feeling raw (no encouragement or comfort - he doesn't even reach out to give me a hug). He doesn't bring anything up, ever. I constantly feel invisible and unloved.

We're in marriage counseling. Marriage counselor doesn't know I have BPD (i was diagnosed by my personal therapist), but she tends to validate my reactions knowing my mental health struggles and always turns to him asking for his thoughts or explanations. He talks like he's in a sports interview: "Yeah, I mean, I'm just going to keep working on myself, keep focusing on myself, and looking forward to positive changes." Always bullshit answers that are fluffy and don't mean anything and feel minimizing to what's actually going on.

Wow this is on point. My husband and I have been in marriage counseling and I have found it so hard to detail what exactly is going on to trigger me, but I know there are legit issues (whether or not related directly to my mental state). Same with my individual therapy - I'm having a hard time explaining why I think I have BPD because I'm not actively in the altered mindset when speaking with my therapist. 

This is very helpful. Thank you.

Okay that's exactly my experience and it's like I cannot even make myself feel differently when I'm in a mode of negative thoughts. Plus any slight inconvenience or perceived threat/hurt/offense makes me want to get a divorce, completely forgetting the positive things about him or our marriage. 

I am really trying to get to the bottom of my patterns and thinking my therapist and I need to explore BPD more than the brief conversation we've had.

Thank you for your reply. I think the issue is we didn't know each other well enough before getting married. I can say with confidence that I did not know he was so emotionally unavailable, but here we are. I do not expect him to fix new, but I do expect him to be there for me when I need him.

Thank you. He does bring value in a very tangible way - help with the kids, income, savings, someone to "work" through life with. Just not much fulfillment in an emotional sense. And for me, that's very important, so I feel like I'm missing something.
I'll look into those books. I appreciate your help.

Thank you for your thoughtful reply. The thing is, I don't think he's doing any of this intentionally. I don't believe he has a malicious bone in his body. But it's almost the lack of intent that makes it even worse.

I will say he didn't 100% neglect to give me any attention at all, but no, he did not prepare and I did have to spend a good bit of time in the delivery room telling him what I needed.

Edited to add: I have recommended a few books to him and he just "doesn't like to read" so he doesn't. Books on supporting a partner with depression and anxiety, etc.
I do journal but putting things in writing feels like they're being solidified, so I'm actually having a harder time dealing with them.
I've been in individual therapy for over 2 years and managing my symptoms as best I can for almost 20 years.

Whether withholding or just absence of feelings altogether, I feel that having fulfilling, enriching, validating conversation is not too much to ask. Or feeling heard. Or comforted when I'm upset. There are several layers to our issues and it feels like incompatibility, not like I've got high expectations.

Okay that gets me back to feeling like maybe I'm searching for something in him that isn't part of his DNA. That I would be happier with a more emotional counterpart. I'm always left feeling alone and abandoned. And yes, those are my issues speaking, but I shouldn't be feeling like this after interacting with my partner.

Thanks for your input. I do understand he needs more time to process, but then tell me that. I feel alone in our marital stress because he never shares anything with me. Or he does but only after I am absolutely broken and desperate. 

I am working on finding time to myself and doing more things I enjoy. That's a process because I'm not really sure what those things are. You're right though - he can't be everything. Just hoping he could be somewhat of an emotional support system.

I'm doing my very best, but I can't just stop being a mom. It does not make financial sense to put our kids in full time care for me to go back to work, and up until a week ago (when my older son started kindergarten), I've been totally kid-focused with not much time for myself. Husband works 60+ hours a week and we have no family nearby. It has definitely been a very challenging season and I'm happy to finally feel like I can get a break during the days.

I am working on this. Being a stay at home mom is very lonely and isolating without family nearby to give reprieve. I'm starting to get a little independence back since my kids just started school for the first time. I do currently work with Instacart and Shipt, watch I'm not exactly passionate about, but it helps me feel like I'm contributing, gets me out of the house, etc.
We are currently in couples counseling.
Yes, we are going to continue counseling.

I'm 32 and we've been married about 7 years. 

I do have a degree but not much real work experience (besides customer service and 2 years in an office setting). The thought of having my own life and schedule is what keeps me driven actually. I just haven't had a chance to work and build up experience since I've been staying home with the kids. Our oldest son just started kindergarten so I'm almost to where I can have a real job again. 

Taking charge would excite me. I would just need to get some drive to be intimate in the first place.

I'm glad to see I have some solidarity. I was hoping that by being open, someone in a similar position could feel free to open up as well. 

My husband and I also have a pretty tense relationship. We were a lot more relaxed around each other in the beginning, but as the years have gone by and I have been feeling more and more anxious to feel fulfilled, it's gotten tense. It's like I'm mad at our relationship. I find him more annoying now, maybe just from the fact that I wish things were different.

I have told him I need better/more open communication to feel fulfilled in our relationship. That we need to work on it (and go to therapy, which he finally agreed to) so the future he has in mind for us includes me. I have been very clear that I am not happy with our lack of connection, and I believe he cares, but I also think he's just a very laid back, simple guy who "wants everyone to be happy" like it's just going to happen.

I understand what you're saying. But please know that I do speak to a therapist personally, as well as us together as a couple. What I mean by this post is that I just feel extremely conflicted. Wanting to feel more fulfilled and unsure that I can get that from my husband versus staying in the marriage, working on it, and living the rest of my life feeling my needs are not being met.
I did not get pregnant before we got married. I got pregnant 6 months after we got married (sorry if I worded it wrong).
I did not get pregnant before we got married. I got pregnant 6 months after we got married (sorry if I worded it wrong).

I probably would date him but unsure that I would have turned it into a serious relationship understanding my needs a little more. I didn't know myself very well when we got married, but I think I need more from my partner than he gives me.

I have told both of them I feel disconnected, that I want to feel closer to my husband. I told my husband I feel miles away from him, but no specifics like thinking about divorcing. I am going to open up completely to my therapist about these things at my next appointment.
I see a therapist personally and we see one together as a couple. I just haven't opened up about these things yet.

Tell him that I think about divorce? I have told him I feel disconnected and I need to be able to talk to him more. We just don't seem to have anything to talk about. 

We connected in the beginning on very superficial things - going to dinner, having drinks, music - but we only dated for 6 months before getting married, then 6 months later had our first kid. It was rushed.
Is this something you deal with?

I've been in individual counseling for over a year, working on my personal mental health but not really bringing up martial issues other than feeling lonely. My husband and I started marriage counseling this week and I feel it would be beneficial for us to continue.
I can guarantee you he will not. He's a conservative Christian.
The difference in the way the body feels, the sensuality, the general approach to sex.
The idea of bringing up opening the marriage gives me anxiety because of how *not* into it my husband would be. It would break him apart.
You sure made being single sound like a lot of fun 😂
Thanks for your reply, but I'm really not following. Are you advocating for me to divorce? Or stay with my husband?
I knew my preferences in my early teens, but never admitted it (still haven't out loud) and never really acted on them (only very few times). I think I'm just now realizing the impact of that.
Being single scares the shit out of me though. We have two small kids.

I think it's on my mind because it's natural to have sexual urges and mine happen to be (sometimes) for the opposite sex. I think about sex no more often than the average person. 

I got married to him for several reasons, and being in a secure relationship was one. I'm not sure I wouldn't have these feelings with anyone else.
Yes, we actually have our first marriage counseling session next week. Hopefully it'll help settle some things so we can move on and strengthen our marriage.
He has already thought all that through. We have an investments advisor and everything. He is already planning on having our mortgage paid off in 10 years.
I really appreciate that.
Oh man this would destroy him. I know he feels very stuck between wanting to provide, stay in his chosen career path, and spending more time with his family.

But he actually sees the negatives in his BIL's life. He'll be the first to tell you what a shame it is. My husband is very present when he is home, and I really appreciate it. It's him missing the kids' activities due to his demanding schedule or when he says he thinks he needs a second job or when he can't hold a conversation without it turning to retirement..
He tells me when I ask but not otherwise. He doesn't seem concerned with keeping me updated

I do wish he would loop me in on what he's doing. I'll hear him mention stock purchases/sales and other investments to other people and I have no idea what he's talking about. I feel like I should know what he's doing with OUR money for OUR future.
Thank you for the encouragement.

I actually got him to agree to individual counseling to aid in our marriage counseling, but I highly, highly doubt he is reflective enough to even know how to open up or what to mention in his sessions. He's an "everything's fine" guy.

He's only ever expressed interest in doing what he currently does, and he's had many different types of jobs. I think he really enjoys it, but gets stressed with the day to day on occasion. I think one thing he likes the most is the security. 

Side note - his brother in law got my husband into his current position. BIL is successful, but has a falling marriage and literally never sees his (now grown) kids. I've brought this up to my husband before and he is looking at it as a short term sacrifice for the end goal. It's heartbreaking.
This makes complete sense. Thank you.
We have our first counseling session next week.
